question.text: Will front-month ICE Brent crude futures (January 2027 contract) settle above $100.00 per barrel on 27 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the ICE Futures Europe official daily settlement price for the Brent Crude January 2027 futures contract (ICE logical code BRN, January 2027 delivery; Barchart symbol CBF27) for the trading session of Friday, 27 November 2026 is greater than $100.00 per barrel, and NO otherwise; a settlement of exactly $100.00 per barrel resolves NO. ICE's official settlement price for this contract and session is displayed as the end-of-day value on the 27 November 2026 row of Barchart's price history page: https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/CBF27/historical-prices. If that page is unavailable or shows no value for the 27 November 2026 session, the ICE settlement price for this contract and session as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used. Where the Barchart figure and ICE's official settlement differ, ICE's official settlement governs.
question.fine_print: If ICE Futures Europe publishes a corrected settlement price for the 27 November 2026 session of this contract, the corrected figure governs.

research:
## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-11-17: I tried to read Barchart's CBF27 historical-prices page, the official resolution source. It returned HTTP 202 with no content because the page is built by scripts, so I could not read any value there. I also could not find an ICE settlement file that I could access. [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/CBF27/historical-prices)
- 2026-11-16: The latest settlement I found is for the January 2027 contract: $92.44, down $3.40 (3.55%) from the 13 November settlement of $95.84. [Infobae/EFE](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/16/el-brent-baja-un-355-hasta-9244-dolares-por-el-auge-de-exportaciones-en-oriente-medio/); [Business Times](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/energy-commodities/oil-settles-lower-recovering-middle-east-exports-bolster-surplus-outlook) (from the news feed, which also gave $92.44 / -$3.40). Yahoo's BZ=F close for the same day was $92.13, slightly different, probably because it is taken at a different time than ICE's settlement.
- To settle above $100.00, the contract needs to rise about 8.2% from $92.44 over 9 trading sessions (17 to 27 November).

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question yet. The price has moved further below the threshold since the 13 November baseline in the question: it was 4-5% below $100 then and is about 8% below now.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-17: Kalshi's Brent market for 17 November (settled on the Pyth feed) puts about a 51% chance on a close above $90. That implies overnight trading around $90, below Monday's settlement (from the market data provided to me).
- 2026-11-16: Brent fell as Strait of Hormuz flows recovered. The IEA now expects a Q4 surplus, with supply of 105 mb/d running 1.7 mb/d above demand; it had earlier forecast a deficit. China's October refinery throughput fell 8.1% year on year. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said mines hit tankers near Hormuz, which Reuters could not verify. BMI said the export recovery is "fragile." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/oil-prices-brent-wti-latest.html)
- 2026-11-16: TradingNEWS reported:
  - The IEA says global observed inventories rose 52 million barrels in October, the first monthly rise since June.
  - Gulf exports are at 60-80% of normal.
  - Brent peaked near $118 on 30 October and is down about 19% since.
  - The dollar index is near a 19-month high, and futures price a 25bp Fed hike in December.
  - The author's base case is a $93-97 range, with $100 reachable only on escalation or a restrained OPEC+ outcome. [TradingNEWS](https://www.tradingnews.com/news/wti-slips-to-88-30-and-brent-to-95-36-as-hormuz-flows-normalize-93-usd-wti-100-usd-brent-targets)
- 2026-11-15: Goldman Sachs expects a 2 mb/d surplus in 2027 and a Brent average of $88 that year, falling to $78 by the end of 2027. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/oil-prices-brent-wti-latest.html)
- 2026-11-13: The IEA published its Oil Market Report pointing to recovering Middle East exports. [Qz](https://qz.com/oil-prices-slip-iea-supply-surplus-iran-war-111626)
- 2026-11-09: Reports of a US-Iran deal came out and were disputed. On 2 November Iran had signaled it was ready to negotiate. [TradingNEWS](https://www.tradingnews.com/news/wti-slips-to-88-30-and-brent-to-95-36-as-hormuz-flows-normalize-93-usd-wti-100-usd-brent-targets)
- Data conflict: the background says Brent spot averaged $124 in October, while TradingNEWS puts the late-October futures peak near $118. Wikipedia's chronology lists Brent at $109.86 on 16 October. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026%E2%80%932028_world_oil_market_chronology)

## 4. Base rates

- Statistical baseline from code, using 3 years of BZ=F 8-day returns from $92.13: p50 $92.46, p75 $96.21, p90 $101.03, p95 $105.36. On that basis, the chance of being above $100 is roughly 10-12%.
- Recent daily moves have often been 3-4% (for example +4% on 1 and 8 October, +4% on 16 October, -3.6% on 16 November). Between 3 and 10 November the price fell from about $98.32 to $91.49, roughly 7% in a week. Between 10 and 13 November it rebounded about 5%, from $91.49 to $95.84. Moves of 8% in two weeks have happened during this conflict, both up and down.
- The trend is down: about 19% below the late-October peak, with inventories building and Hormuz flows recovering.

## 5. Other forecasts

- Kalshi, Brent on 30 November at 5pm EST (Pyth feed, a different date and price source from this question), prices as of 2026-11-17: above $95.99 at 18%, above $97.99 at 14%. There was no $99.99 strike in the data I received; extrapolating, above $100 would be roughly 10-12%. These prices may have been set before Monday's late-session drop.
- Polymarket: I could not find a matching Brent market for November.
- EIA STEO (10 November) expects Brent spot "near $100" for the rest of 2026, with a 2026 average of $97.44. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/global_oil.php)
- Goldman Sachs expects a $88 average for 2027 (see above).

## 6. Upcoming events before 27 November

- 17 November: US retail sales and industrial production; API inventory estimate. [TradingNEWS](https://www.tradingnews.com/news/wti-slips-to-88-30-and-brent-to-95-36-as-hormuz-flows-normalize-93-usd-wti-100-usd-brent-targets)
- 18 November: EIA Petroleum Status Report; FOMC minutes.
- This week: Trump-Xi talks focused on trade and technology. OPEC+'s capacity review, which feeds into the 2027 quotas, was delayed to mid-November.
- Ongoing: US-Iran diplomacy, any US blockade of Iran, and tanker or mine attacks in or near Hormuz. Any of these is the most likely trigger for a sharp move up.
- 25 November (expected): next EIA weekly report, likely moved earlier because of the US Thanksgiving holiday on 26 November. I have not verified this. Trading on Friday 27 November may be thin.
- 29 November: the OPEC+ ministerial meeting on 2027 quotas comes after the resolution date, but positioning ahead of it could move prices. 30 November is the January contract's expiry.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain, with roughly 9 trading sessions from 17 to 27 November. YES requires the ICE settlement of the January 2027 Brent contract on Friday 27 November to be above $100.00. The last confirmed settlement was $92.44 on 16 November, so that means a gain of about 8.2%. Overnight Kalshi pricing hints the market may be nearer $90, which would make the required gain about 11%.

(b) If nothing changed, the contract would settle around $90-92, well below $100. The status quo outcome is NO.

(c) Base rate: across 3 years of 8-session Brent returns, the 90th percentile from $92.13 is about $101. That gives roughly a 10-12% chance of finishing above $100. Starting from about $90 instead, it falls to roughly 7-8%. This conflict has produced unusually high volatility, with 7-8% weekly swings in both directions, so the fat tails are real.

(d) Evidence for each side:
- **For YES:**
  - Tanker and mine attacks near Hormuz are continuing, including the IRGC's 16 November claims.
  - BMI calls the export recovery "fragile."
  - On 10 November the EIA said it expects Brent "near $100" for the rest of 2026.
  - The market rebounded 5% between 10 and 13 November, showing it can move fast.
- **For NO:**
  - On 13 November the IEA flipped its Q4 outlook to a 1.7 mb/d surplus, and inventories rose 52 mb in October.
  - Hormuz flows are recovering, and Iran-Oman corridor talks are under way.
  - Goldman (15 November) is bearish.
  - The dollar is strong.
  - The price fell 3.55% on 16 November, and overnight Kalshi pricing implies a further drop toward $90.
  - Kalshi's 30 November market prices "above $97.99" at only 14%, which implies about 10% for above $100. Those prices were possibly set before Monday's decline.

(e) Scenarios:
- **NO:** Gulf exports keep normalizing, US stocks build, and Thanksgiving trading is thin. January Brent drifts at $87-95 into the 27 November settlement.
- **YES:** A major tanker strike or a collapse of the US-Iran or Iran-Oman talks re-closes Hormuz flows. Brent jumps 4-6% on two separate headline days, and the January contract squeezes above $100 ahead of expiry and the OPEC+ meeting.

(f) I start from the roughly 10% statistical and Kalshi anchor. I move down modestly because:
- The latest price is likely lower than the anchor assumes, around $90.
- The trend and fundamentals (surplus, inventories building) are bearish.
- The Kalshi strikes may be stale.

Geopolitical tail risk keeps the estimate from going much lower.

Probability: 7%

(a) About 10 days remain, ending at the ICE settlement on Friday 27 November 2026 (around 19:30 London). For YES, the January 2027 Brent contract must settle above $100.00. It settled at $92.44 on 16 November and may be trading nearer $90 overnight, so it needs a gain of roughly 8-11% in 8-9 sessions.

(b) If nothing changes, the price stays around $90-93 and the question resolves NO.

(c) Base rate: the empirical distribution of 8-session Brent returns over the last 3 years, starting from $92.13, puts $100 near the 88th-90th percentile, so about 10-12%. Starting nearer $90, it is closer to 8-9%. Volatility during the current conflict is above the 3-year average, which thickens both tails.
